subject: Geography
central_question: How do transport and communication connect producing centres, consuming centres and people across the world?
in_scope_units: Role of transport, communication and trade in linking places.
Transport networks, modes and the development of land transport.
Roads, highways, traffic flows and border roads.
Railways and major regional and trans-continental railway systems.
Water transport, sea routes, shipping canals and inland waterways.
Air transport and inter-continental air routes.
Communications, optic fibre, satellites, the internet and cyberspace.
banned_topics: Detailed organisation of retail and wholesale trade as tertiary activities.
Balance of trade, WTO and classification of ports by trade function.

known_pitfalls.claim: One transport mode is always superior to all others.
known_pitfalls.correction: The suitable mode depends on the goods, distance, cost and available facilities; in a well-managed system the modes complement one another.

known_pitfalls.claim: A transport network consists only of roads or railway lines.
known_pitfalls.correction: A network is a pattern of places or nodes joined by routes or links and can be formed by several transport modes.

known_pitfalls.claim: Communication still always requires physical transport of messages.
known_pitfalls.correction: Mobile telephony, optic fibre, satellites and the internet transmit information without physically moving the sender and receiver.
